public_rationale: CoreWeave's annual results establish losses at an important provider. They do not establish the economics of GPU rental throughout the sector. Adjusted measures also differ from the unadjusted figures. The evidence is consistent with Zitron's concern, but its company, segment and accounting coverage is insufficient to settle his broader claim.
limitations: Individual provider losses are not a measured sector margin.
Positive adjusted margins are not equivalent to profits after all relevant costs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPU compute rental is a low- or negative-margin business.

statement.excerpt: All evidence points to GPU compute either being a low or negative-margin business.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies the business as renting GPU compute, excluding hardware sales.
The ordinary reading concerns profitability after operating costs, including depreciation. Net profitability also reflects the financing costs discussed in the post.
I use calendar 2025 because the adjacent supporting example expressly describes 2025. This is a contextual choice for an otherwise undated sector observation.
Low has no numerical threshold. I will not invent one or treat adjusted EBITDA as interchangeable with operating or net profit.
Company-wide results from individual providers are informative but cannot alone establish GPU rental margins across the sector.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable disclosures covering a representative share of GPU rental activity show consistently low or negative margins after the relevant costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable disclosures establish substantial GPU rental activity earning clearly strong margins after the same costs, undermining the asserted sector-wide pattern.
